description:
`is_public_compiler2_trace_event` (`telemetry/jsonl.rs:793`) allowlists three
event names that nothing emits:

    ["fz", "compiler2", "work", "started"]
    ["fz", "compiler2", "pull", "phase", ..]
    ["fz", "compiler2", "drive", "stalled"]

Confirmed two ways: no emit site anywhere in `src/`, and 0 occurrences of each in
a real 17,574-event public log (`--log-telemetry`, 00420_enum_take_drop_split).

A dead allowlist row reads as "this signal exists and was empty this run", which
is worse than its absence -- it sends an investigator looking for a switch to
turn on.

## `drive.stalled` looks like a rename that lost its other half

The emitted event is `fz.compiler2.drive.demand_on_stall` (`drive.rs:497`,
projected at `jsonl.rs:371`), carrying `(&usize producer_pokes,
&HashSet<FactKey> demanded_facts)`. It is NOT allowlisted, so the public log
cannot see stall behaviour at all while advertising a `drive.stalled` row that
never fires.

Note fz-kdt.34 wants exactly that payload for its "work-start reason and exact
demanded fact/product" contract line, so allowlisting `demand_on_stall` may land
there instead; this ticket then just deletes the three dead rows.

## Checks

- Every allowlist row has an emitter, proven by a test that fails when a row has
  none (walk the allowlist, assert each name is emitted somewhere) -- otherwise
  this regrows.
- The three rows are deleted, or their emitters written.
title: Three public-trace allowlist rows have no emitter anywhere in the tree
